transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I've been feeling deeply depressed and sad for the past three weeks. It feels like I'm constantly in a gloomy mood and I just can't seem to shake it.
Have you ever had periods in your life lasting at least a few days where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, happy, or hyperactive, perhaps needing very little sleep?
No, I've never experienced periods like that. I have never felt unusually energetic, hyperactive, or felt like I didn't need to sleep.
Did these feelings of depression start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life, or did they seem to come out of nowhere?

I'm not really sure of any specific cause. These feelings just seemed to come out of nowhere about three weeks ago. There wasn't any major life change or stressful event that I can think of that triggered it.
During these past few weeks, have you heard or seen things that others couldn't, or held any strong beliefs that other people told you were not true?
No, I haven't seen or heard anything strange that wasn't really there. I also haven't held any unusual beliefs that other people found strange or disagreed with.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy doing, like hobbies, work, or spending time with family?

Yes, I really have. Over the past three weeks, I've completely lost interest in the hobbies and activities I used to love. Even when I try to force myself to do them, I just don't feel any joy or pleasure from them anymore.
How has your sleep been over these past three weeks? Have you had trouble sleeping, or have you been sleeping much more than usual?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep patterns over the past three weeks. It seems to be pretty much the same as usual.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking in energy over the last three weeks, even when you haven't been doing much?
I haven't particularly noticed feeling unusually tired or lacking in physical energy. My physical energy levels seem to be pretty much the same as they always have been.
Have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt over the past three weeks?
No, I haven't really felt that way. I don't think I have experienced those specific feelings of worthlessness or guilt over the past few weeks.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, such as eating much less or much more than usual?
No, I haven't noticed any significant changes in my appetite or my weight recently. I've been eating about the same as I normally do.
Have you found it harder than usual to concentrate, focus on tasks, or make decisions over the last three weeks?
No, I haven't really noticed any difficulties with concentrating or making decisions lately. My focus and ability to make choices seem to be about the same as they normally are.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a three-week history of persistent depressed mood and a complete loss of interest or pleasure in activities (anhedonia). These represent two core symptoms of a major depressive episode. There is no history of manic or hypomanic symptoms, psychotic features, or clear psychosocial stressors, making Major Depressive Disorder the most appropriate diagnosis.
